phases.name: Define event meaning and safe ingestion
phases.description: Separate the frozen workload from assumptions, define retry-safe event identity, and build a durable path that can absorb bursts.

phases.name: Publish real-time metrics and definitions
phases.description: Produce the sub-minute stream view while keeping event schemas, custom measures, and conversion definitions versioned.

phases.name: Build the batch and historical path
phases.description: Retain raw events under an approved policy and load them into a warehouse for historical and complex analysis.

phases.name: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
phases.description: Connect common-query pre-aggregation and report APIs to both real-time and historical data, and observe correctness and freshness.

phases.name: Review exactness and unresolved policies
phases.description: Make sampling and retention boundaries explicit and identify decisions that need product or policy approval.

steps.phase: Define event meaning and safe ingestion
steps.title: Mark brief facts and open decisions
steps.content: Brief facts: collect user events and page views; provide real-time and historical analytics, custom reports, segmentation, funnels, goals, conversions, custom dimensions and metrics, and exports; handle billions of events per day; process real-time data in less than one minute; tolerate spikes; count and aggregate accurately; answer complex queries; and follow retention policies. The stated scale and freshness values are acceptance targets, not demonstrated capacity or a proven result. The brief does not define event identity, what constitutes a unique person or session, event lateness, peak rate, dimension cardinality, query latency, or any retention duration. The architecture choices in this walkthrough are assumptions to review, not additional brief facts.

steps.phase: Define event meaning and safe ingestion
steps.title: Choose retry-safe event counting semantics
steps.content: Assumption to validate: an accepted event has a stable event_id created before retries. Count accepted page-view and named-event records separately, and deduplicate a repeated event_id so delivery retries do not increment an aggregate twice. Do not treat event counts as unique people, sessions, or conversions; those need their own identity, session, and goal rules. The brief does not specify those rules or how long retry identities must remain available.

decision.question: What is the counting unit for events and page views?
decision.chosen: Count accepted event records by event type and use a stable event_id for idempotent retry deduplication; define people, sessions, and conversion attribution as separate product semantics.
decision.chosenReason: This protects accurate aggregation from transport retries without inventing a user identity or claiming exactly-once delivery. The event ID format and deduplication horizon remain assumptions to ratify.

alternatives.option: Increment every time an event is delivered
alternatives.tradeoff: Retries and replay can overcount events.

alternatives.option: Count every event as a unique person or session
alternatives.tradeoff: Event volume does not establish person or session identity.

steps.phase: Define event meaning and safe ingestion
steps.title: Choose the batch and stream split
steps.content: Use the hint's Lambda-style split as an architecture assumption: a stream path publishes current metrics against the stated less-than-one-minute constraint, while a batch path rebuilds and queries history from retained raw events in the warehouse. Both paths consume the same accepted event record and schema version. Batch results are not used to claim real-time freshness.

decision.question: How should real-time and historical analytics share event data?
decision.chosen: Fan out the durable event log to stream processing for current metrics and to retained raw storage for batch loading into the historical warehouse.
decision.chosenReason: The brief asks for both real-time and historical analytics and names batch plus stream processing. A shared durable input makes rebuild and comparison possible.

alternatives.option: Run every dashboard query over the raw event log
alternatives.tradeoff: Repeated large scans make interactive and historical queries compete with ingestion.

alternatives.option: Use only streaming state for all history
alternatives.tradeoff: It does not provide the requested warehouse-backed historical analysis or a clean rebuild source.

steps.phase: Define event meaning and safe ingestion
steps.title: Add browser and app event clients
steps.content: Represent the browser and app SDKs that report page views and named events. The stable event_id is an explicit design assumption from the counting decision; include event time, event type, tenant or site scope, schema version, and only consent-permitted identity fields. Do not infer an identity policy from the brief.

component.label: Browser / App Analytics SDK
component.description: Reports page views and user events

properties.purpose: Emit page-view and named-event records with a stable retry identity, event time, event type, tenant or site scope, schema version, and consent-permitted identity fields; preserve the same event identity on retry.

component.highlightReason: The Web App catalog component represents the client SDK without introducing a new client type.

steps.phase: Define event meaning and safe ingestion
steps.title: Add a validated event-ingestion boundary
steps.content: Accept SDK events through the API boundary. Validate tenant authorization, event type, schema version, payload shape, and event identity before acknowledging. Return retryable backpressure when durable enqueue is unavailable; the acknowledgement must not imply that the real-time aggregate is already visible.

component.label: Analytics Event Ingestion API
component.description: Validates and durably accepts client events

properties.purpose: Authenticate the tenant or site, validate event identity and the registered schema version, reject malformed payloads, and acknowledge only after durable enqueue; expose retryable backpressure instead of silently dropping events.

component.highlightReason: API Gateway is the existing catalog request boundary and exposes validation, authentication, and throttling controls.

steps.phase: Define event meaning and safe ingestion
steps.title: Send client events to ingestion
steps.content: The client retries an unconfirmed event with the same event_id. Keep tenant authorization and schema validation at the API boundary, and report acceptance separately from later aggregate freshness.

connection.label: Page views + named events
connection.description: Authenticated event records retain their retry identity and schema version

steps.phase: Define event meaning and safe ingestion
steps.title: Add a durable event buffer
steps.content: Use the catalog Message Broker to absorb traffic spikes and decouple API acceptance from stream and batch consumers. Select partitioning from the ordering and isolation contract after those are defined; the brief supplies no partition count, retention duration, or peak-rate target.

component.label: Durable Analytics Event Log
component.description: Buffers events for independent stream and batch consumers

properties.purpose: Persist accepted event records, absorb traffic spikes, expose consumer lag, and allow independent stream and raw-history consumers to replay; choose partitioning and retention only after ordering, recovery, and policy requirements are agreed.

component.highlightReason: Message Broker is the existing catalog concept for durable event distribution and burst decoupling.

steps.phase: Define event meaning and safe ingestion
steps.title: Acknowledge only after durable enqueue
steps.content: The API publishes validated events to the durable log and acknowledges only after enqueue confirmation. On broker pressure, preserve the same event identity for retry and surface backpressure so accepted-event counts remain auditable.

connection.label: Validated durable event
connection.description: The queue buffers bursts and supports consumer recovery without changing event identity

steps.phase: Define event meaning and safe ingestion
steps.title: Add event-time stream processing
steps.content: Deduplicate transport retries by event_id, maintain exact event and page-view aggregates, and publish event-time progress for the real-time path. Apply state updates idempotently before advancing consumer checkpoints. Define late-event correction and deduplication retention with the product owner; neither is quantified in the brief.

component.label: Event-Time Metrics Processor

properties.purpose: Deduplicate stable event identities, maintain exact page-view and named-event aggregates, compute configured goals and conversion inputs, attach event-time freshness markers, and checkpoint only after an idempotent state update; define late-event correction before production.

component.highlightReason: Stream Processor is an existing catalog component for event-time processing and stateful metrics.

steps.phase: Define event meaning and safe ingestion
steps.title: Consume and recover events from the log
steps.content: The stream processor consumes replayable records and commits dedupe state and aggregate updates before acknowledging a batch or checkpoint. Monitor consumer lag and event age against the stated less-than-one-minute freshness requirement; do not substitute an unstated latency target.

connection.label: Replayable event-time records
connection.description: Stable event identities support idempotent replay and accurate aggregation

steps.phase: Define event meaning and safe ingestion
steps.title: Choose how the pipeline absorbs spikes
steps.content: Treat burst handling as an explicit design assumption: let the durable log buffer temporary producer surges, scale stream consumers using observed lag and safe state ownership, and apply backpressure before acknowledging data that was not persisted. Validate capacity and scaling behavior with the actual traffic shape; the brief gives no peak rate or numeric scaling thresholds.

decision.question: How should ingestion preserve events during traffic spikes?
decision.chosen: Buffer accepted events durably, scale consumers from measured lag within safe partition ownership, and surface retryable backpressure when the durable boundary is saturated.
decision.chosenReason: This separates burst absorption from processing speed while keeping acknowledgement and event loss observable. Capacity remains a workload-validation task.

alternatives.option: Acknowledge before enqueue to protect API latency
alternatives.tradeoff: A process or broker failure can lose an event already reported as accepted.

alternatives.option: Scale workers without checking partition or state ownership
alternatives.tradeoff: More workers do not fix an ordering bottleneck and can duplicate state ownership.

steps.phase: Publish real-time metrics and definitions
steps.title: Add the real-time aggregate store
steps.content: Publish current exact event counts and configured metric results with their event-time boundary and schema version. Keep these aggregates separate from unique-person and session claims until identity semantics are approved; do not hide stale or corrected results.

component.label: Real-Time Analytics Aggregates
component.description: Current event, funnel, and conversion metrics

properties.purpose: Serve current exact page-view and event aggregates plus configured segmentation, funnel, and conversion measures; include event-time freshness, schema version, correction status, and whether a result is exact or sampled.

component.highlightReason: Analytics is the existing catalog concept for event metrics, aggregations, and business intelligence.

steps.phase: Publish real-time metrics and definitions
steps.title: Publish stream aggregates with freshness
steps.content: Write completed aggregate updates with their event-time boundary and schema version. Compare event acceptance time to aggregate availability so the less-than-one-minute requirement is measured end to end, including backlog and correction work.

connection.label: Exact current aggregates + freshness
connection.description: Published values carry event-time and schema context for honest real-time reads

steps.phase: Publish real-time metrics and definitions
steps.title: Add a versioned analytics-definition registry
steps.content: Store tenant-scoped event schemas, custom dimension definitions, metric formulas and units, goal definitions, and the approved identity and retention policies. Validate schema versions at ingestion and processing. The brief does not specify dimension cardinality limits, conversion attribution, or goal windows, so leave those values for product review.

component.label: Schema, Metrics, and Goal Registry
component.description: Versioned tenant analytics definitions and policies

properties.purpose: Persist tenant-scoped versioned event schemas, custom dimensions, metric formulas and units, goal definitions, identity semantics, and approved retention and export policies; preserve definition versions used to produce each aggregate.

component.highlightReason: Database is an existing catalog persistence concept for versioned analytics configuration; no custom node is needed.

steps.phase: Publish real-time metrics and definitions
steps.title: Resolve definitions before aggregation
steps.content: The processor reads the registered schema and goal versions used by each event. Unknown or incompatible versions must be visible as rejected or unresolved input, not silently coerced into a different metric definition.

connection.label: Versioned schema + goal lookup
connection.description: Processing records which registered definitions shaped each result

steps.phase: Publish real-time metrics and definitions
steps.title: Apply segmentation, funnels, and conversion definitions
steps.content: Assumption to review: represent segments and funnel steps as versioned predicates over approved event dimensions, and calculate conversions from an explicit goal definition. Require the product owner to decide person or session identity, step ordering, conversion window, attribution, and treatment of late events before interpreting these as user-level outcomes.

properties.purpose: Serve exact event aggregates and versioned segment, funnel, and goal-conversion results. Use only registered custom dimensions and metric formulas; retain schema version, identity semantics, event-time freshness, correction status, and exact-or-sampled status with each result. User or session identity, funnel ordering, conversion window, and attribution require product approval.

steps.phase: Build the batch and historical path
steps.title: Add retained raw-event storage
steps.content: Keep replayable raw event records in object storage so batch jobs can rebuild historical aggregates and exports can be materialized. Apply the approved retention and deletion policy across raw data and derived copies; do not choose a duration that the brief does not provide.

component.label: Raw Event History and Export Files
component.description: Replayable event input and generated export artifacts

properties.componentName: Raw Event History and Export Files
properties.purpose: Retain replayable raw events and generated export artifacts under the approved tenant retention and deletion policy; preserve schema and event-time metadata and enforce tenant-scoped access to stored data.

component.highlightReason: Object Storage is the existing catalog concept for durable raw history and export artifacts.

steps.phase: Build the batch and historical path
steps.title: Archive the accepted event stream
steps.content: Write the same accepted, schema-versioned records to raw history. Keep the archive independent of stream state so it can support batch recomputation, retention enforcement, and export generation.

connection.label: Replayable raw event records
connection.description: The durable history is the batch rebuild and export source

steps.phase: Build the batch and historical path
steps.title: Add the historical analytics warehouse
steps.content: Use the warehouse for historical reports, large scans, cohort and funnel analysis, and recomputation from retained raw events. Choose physical partitioning and query limits from representative tenant queries and measured data; no warehouse size, query-latency goal, or retention duration is stated.

component.label: Historical Analytics Warehouse
component.description: Batch-built store for complex historical queries

properties.purpose: Store batch-built historical event aggregates and queryable dimensions for complex reports, cohorts, and funnels; preserve definition versions and event-time boundaries, and set physical layout and retention only from reviewed workloads and policy.

component.highlightReason: Data Warehouse is the existing catalog concept for OLAP and historical analysis.

steps.phase: Build the batch and historical path
steps.title: Load raw events into historical tables
steps.content: Batch jobs read retained raw records and build historical tables and rollups for reports and approved segment or funnel analyses, using the same versioned event and metric definitions as the stream path. Make late corrections and rebuild status visible so historical totals can be compared with current aggregates.

connection.label: Batch loads + historical rollups
connection.description: Rebuildable warehouse tables retain event-time and definition-version context

steps.phase: Build the batch and historical path
steps.title: Make historical reports schema-aware
steps.content: Use the same tenant-scoped custom dimensions and versioned metric definitions for historical segmentation and funnels. High-cardinality behavior and backfill semantics are open workload decisions; measure representative queries and preserve raw events so a reviewed definition change can be rebuilt deliberately.

properties.purpose: Serve historical custom reports, cohorts, and funnels using tenant-scoped registered dimensions and versioned metric formulas; preserve event-time and definition versions for reproducible backfills. Determine high-cardinality handling, query guardrails, and physical layout from measured workloads rather than invented limits.

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Add a cache for common query results
steps.content: Pre-aggregate or cache common dashboard queries by tenant, query definition, schema version, and source freshness. Keep the analytics stores authoritative and return the result's freshness and exact-or-sampled status with cached responses.

component.label: Common Analytics Query Cache
component.description: Reusable pre-aggregates for frequent dashboard queries

properties.purpose: Cache or pre-aggregate frequent tenant-scoped query results by definition and schema version; carry source freshness and exact-or-sampled status, and never make cached values the source of truth.

component.highlightReason: Cache is an existing catalog component for common-query acceleration; no cache duration or capacity is assumed.

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Pre-aggregate common real-time queries
steps.content: Populate reusable cache entries from published stream aggregates. Invalidate or version entries when late-event corrections or metric-definition changes alter their meaning.

connection.label: Versioned common-query results
connection.description: Pre-aggregates retain the source freshness and metric-definition version

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Add the report and export API
steps.content: Provide tenant-authorized report queries and dashboard data over real-time aggregates and historical warehouse tables. Validate custom metric definitions, expose freshness and sampling status, and create asynchronous export jobs for large result sets rather than making an interactive request wait for a full export.

component.label: Reports and Export Service
component.description: Authorizes dashboards, custom reports, and export jobs

properties.purpose: Authorize tenant-scoped dashboard and custom-report queries across current aggregates and historical warehouse data; validate registered dimensions and metrics, return freshness and exact-or-sampled status, and schedule large exports for controlled delivery.

component.highlightReason: Backend Server is an existing catalog service concept for report orchestration and export-job APIs.

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Read current metrics for reports
steps.content: The report service queries current aggregates with their event-time watermark. A response must not label an older or corrected generation as current; use the freshness marker measured against the stated real-time constraint.

connection.label: Current aggregates + freshness
connection.description: Report responses expose the published event-time boundary and correction state

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Query historical warehouse data
steps.content: Run complex historical report, segment, and funnel queries against warehouse data using the registered metric and dimension versions. Enforce tenant scope and query guardrails chosen from workload evidence, and make incomplete or retention-expired results explicit.

connection.label: Historical report queries
connection.description: Warehouse queries use versioned definitions and explicit retention boundaries

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Look up cached common queries
steps.content: The report service may use a matching cache entry before querying its source. A hit is usable only with its tenant, definition version, freshness marker, and exact-or-sampled status; cache misses fall through to the current aggregate or warehouse.

connection.label: Common-query lookup
connection.description: Only entries with matching tenant and definition context can be reused

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Read approved report definitions
steps.content: Resolve each report's tenant-scoped dimensions, metric formulas, goals, and policy versions from the registry. Enforce authorization before returning results or starting exports.

connection.label: Authorized metric + goal definitions
connection.description: Report execution uses the approved schema and policy versions

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Add the analytics dashboard
steps.content: Give users a dashboard for custom reports, segments, funnels, and goal conversions. Show the selected date range, event-time freshness, metric definition, and whether a view is exact or sampled so users can interpret results correctly.

component.label: User Analytics Dashboard
component.description: Custom reports, segments, funnels, and goals

properties.purpose: Render tenant-authorized custom reports, segments, funnels, and goal conversions with selected time range, metric definition, freshness, and exact-or-sampled status visible to the user.

component.highlightReason: The Web App catalog component represents the user-facing dashboard using an existing frontend concept.

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Connect dashboard queries to the report API
steps.content: Send authenticated dashboard queries and report selections to the API. Keep query execution, metric validation, and export authorization on the service side rather than trusting browser-provided definitions.

connection.label: Dashboard queries + report results
connection.description: The service validates and authorizes report definitions for the tenant

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Write authorized export artifacts
steps.content: The report service materializes an authorized export to object storage and returns a tenant-scoped retrieval path. Apply the approved export-artifact retention and deletion policy; the brief does not specify a file format, size limit, or expiry duration.

connection.label: Authorized export artifact
connection.description: Generated files use tenant-scoped access and the approved artifact lifecycle policy

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Add pipeline and query monitoring
steps.content: Observe accepted and rejected events, queue age, consumer lag, deduplication and correction counts, aggregate freshness, warehouse query health, and export completion. Alert against the brief's freshness requirement and agreed operational policies without inventing numeric thresholds.

component.label: Analytics Pipeline Observability
component.description: Tracks freshness, correctness, query health, and backlog

properties.purpose: Track event acceptance and rejection, queue age, consumer lag, duplicate handling, late corrections, aggregate freshness, warehouse query health, and export completion; set alert thresholds from the stated freshness requirement and reviewed operations policy.

component.highlightReason: Monitoring is an existing catalog concept for operational metrics and alerts.

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Observe broker pressure and accepted events
steps.content: Export received and accepted event rates alongside queue age, enqueue rejection, replay, and consumer lag signals. Compare measured daily volume with the brief's target of billions of events per day; validate burst headroom separately because peak rate is unspecified. These signals expose traffic spikes before an accepted event is lost or stream freshness falls behind.

connection.label: Event rate + queue age + replay + rejection metrics
connection.description: Broker pressure and recovery are visible to operators

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Observe exactness and real-time freshness
steps.content: Publish processor event age, deduplication outcomes, correction state, checkpoint health, and aggregate publication time. Compare the full accepted-event-to-visible-metric path with the stated less-than-one-minute constraint.

connection.label: Event age + exactness + checkpoint health
connection.description: Operators can distinguish stale output from duplicate or corrected events

steps.phase: Serve reports, dashboards, exports, and operations
steps.title: Observe historical queries and retention outcomes
steps.content: Track warehouse query behavior, batch completion, rebuild status, and policy-driven expiry or deletion. Review these measures against representative large-dataset queries and the approved retention contract.

connection.label: Batch + query + lifecycle health
connection.description: Historical analysis and retention enforcement remain observable

steps.phase: Review exactness and unresolved policies
steps.title: Keep sampling out of authoritative counts
steps.content: The brief's sampling hint is an option for high-traffic exploratory queries, not permission to silently approximate accurate counts. Assumption to review: keep event totals and configured conversion aggregates exact; allow sampling only when a report explicitly accepts approximation, and expose its sample basis and status. Decide which report classes may be sampled with product owners.

decision.question: Where, if anywhere, may high-traffic analytics use sampling?
decision.chosen: Do not sample authoritative event counts or conversions; permit only explicitly requested exploratory sampling with visible sample status and basis.
decision.chosenReason: This preserves the stated accurate-counting constraint while retaining sampling as an opt-in query-cost tradeoff from the brief's hints.

alternatives.option: Sample every high-volume metric without marking it
alternatives.tradeoff: Users cannot distinguish an estimate from the accurate totals the brief requests.

alternatives.option: Never allow sampling for any exploratory query
alternatives.tradeoff: Some large ad hoc queries may consume more resources than users need to spend.

steps.phase: Review exactness and unresolved policies
steps.title: Leave retention and identity policy values open
steps.content: The brief requires retention policies but supplies no duration or deletion contract. Assumption to review: apply an approved policy consistently to broker replay, raw events, stream deduplication state, warehouse data, cached results, and export artifacts, including derived copies and deletion requests. The product and policy owners must set durations, legal holds, erasure behavior, and the event-retry horizon before expiry is configured.

decision.question: What data lifecycle should the system enforce?
decision.chosen: Use a versioned, approved retention and deletion policy across raw, processed, cached, and exported data; leave every duration and erasure rule unset until the responsible owners decide.
decision.chosenReason: This makes the retention constraint actionable without inventing a duration or claiming compliance with an unspecified policy.

alternatives.option: Choose one default retention duration in the walkthrough
alternatives.tradeoff: The brief gives no period, legal basis, tenant variation, or deletion requirement to justify that value.
This does not implement a retention policy and can conflict with future deletion requirements.

steps.phase: Review exactness and unresolved policies
steps.title: Validate the design against real workload evidence
steps.content: Before implementation, confirm the event identity and session rules, ordering and late-arrival semantics, custom-dimension cardinality, peak traffic shape, query mix, conversion attribution, export contract, and retention policy. Then measure accepted-event loss, duplicate correction, aggregate accuracy, end-to-end freshness against less than one minute, spike recovery, and representative warehouse queries. The brief's stated scale target (billions of events per day) and real-time bound (less than one minute) are acceptance inputs to validate, not achieved guarantees; query latency, peak throughput, and retention duration remain unspecified.
